scene.bubble: Welcome to B2! We're reading Oliver Twist. Learn mixed conditionals — and master key word transformations.
scene.intro: Welcome to Grade 10 and to B2 First. This year the Inspiring Nordic project asks harder questions about society and fairness. In this unit you read what our club thinks about Dickens's Oliver Twist, you learn mixed conditionals to connect a past cause with a present result, and you practise the key word transformation task from the exam. How much does our past decide our present? Let's explore it.

activities.title: Reading — the reading club on Oliver Twist

data.title: Oliver Twist: the past in the present
data.author: mateo
data.text:
Our Grade 10 reading club has begun Oliver Twist by Charles Dickens, and it has started some serious conversations. Oliver is an orphan who grows up in poverty and cruelty, yet somehow stays gentle and honest.

The novel raises an uncomfortable question: how much does our past decide our present? If Oliver had been born into a rich family, he wouldn't be suffering now. If society cared more about poor children, thousands of Olivers wouldn't exist today. These are 'mixed conditionals' — a past cause with a present result.

In our discussion, Nadia argued that circumstances are powerful but not everything. “If Oliver were a weaker person,” she said, “he would have given up long ago.” Liam added that we shouldn't judge people without knowing their story: “If I had grown up like Oliver, I might not be so confident today.”

Dickens wrote the book to change minds. In his time, many people believed the poor deserved their poverty. He wanted readers to feel the injustice — and to act.

Almost two hundred years later, the question remains. If we understood each other's stories better, our world would be kinder. That is a conditional worth making real.

data.title: Mixed conditionals
data.intro: A mixed conditional combines two time frames: usually a past condition with a present result, or a present condition with a past result.

examples.text: If Oliver had been born rich, he wouldn't be poor now.
If I were braver, I would have said something.
If they had listened, things would be different today.

rules: Past cause → present result: If + past perfect, would + verb (now).
Present cause → past result: If + past simple, would have + participle.
Mixed conditionals are common when a past event still affects the present.

items.sentence: If she had studied medicine, she ___ a doctor now.
If I weren't so tired, I ___ to the party last night.
If he had saved money, he ___ his own workshop today.
If we understood each other, there ___ fewer problems now.
If they had planned better, we ___ lost yesterday.

activities.title: Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations

data.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the KEY WORD. Write between two and five words.

items.first: Oliver is poor now because he was born into a poor family.
items.second_end: into a rich family, he wouldn't be poor now.

She didn't train, so she isn't fit now.
They didn't listen, so we have this problem today.

items.first: I'm tired now because I went to bed very late.

data.script: Good morning, Grade 10. This term we're reading Oliver Twist. Dickens wrote it to show the injustice of poverty. Remember our theme: how the past shapes the present. For Friday, prepare a mixed conditional about Oliver — for example, if he had been born rich, he wouldn't be suffering. Nadia will lead the debate, and we'll compare the book with the modern world. Bring your best argument!

activities.title: Speaking — discuss society. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, discuss using mixed conditionals. Model: “If I had grown up in another country, I would probably speak a different language now.” 1) How would your life be different now if you had been born somewhere else? 2) If schools taught one more subject, what should it be, and why? 3) If people understood each other's stories better, would the world really be kinder? Give reasons and examples, then record your discussion.

homework.prompt: Write an opinion paragraph (8–10 sentences) responding to Oliver Twist: does our past decide our present? Use at least three mixed conditionals (e.g. 'If society had cared more, fewer children would suffer today.'). Support your view with reasons. Capital letters and full stops!
